subject: Charter Ethics and Financial Disclosure Requirements
overview: The subcommittee evaluated research on municipal ethics policies and considered how Medford should integrate financial disclosure requirements into its charter. They agreed to present two options to the full committee regarding mandatory disclosure statements and the possible creation of a local ethics commission.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The subcommittee approved the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: Research on Municipal Ethics Provisions
items.summary: Eunice Browne presented research on several Massachusetts cities, finding that only Framingham includes ethics and financial disclosure requirements directly in its charter.

items.title: Discussion on Local Ethics Requirements
items.summary: Maury Carroll reported that former city officials cautioned that additional local requirements might duplicate state law or discourage residents from running for office. The subcommittee discussed whether to focus charter language narrowly on financial transparency or more broadly on ethics oversight.

items.title: Recommendations to Full Committee
items.summary: The subcommittee agreed to present two options to the full committee on August 1st: requiring annual financial disclosure statements by ordinance or mandating the creation of an ethics commission to manage those disclosures. This approach aims to gauge the full committee's support for local ethics requirements before the subcommittee drafts specific charter language.
